name: Micro Eazy
description: A two-sided credit ecosystem: licensed lenders on one side, Kenyan borrowers on the other, and a consent-gated exchange between them.
$comment: THIS FILE IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE ECOSYSTEM.
Every orchestration script reads it and nothing hard-codes a path, a port or a
command anywhere else. That is the whole design: adding a seventh system is one
entry here plus one `git submodule add`, and it appears in `npm run dev`,
`npm run build`, `npm run doctor` and the README map without another edit.
PORTS ARE ASSIGNED HERE, ONCE. Two systems that both default to 3000 is the
single most common way a local ecosystem stops booting, and the fix has to live
somewhere that both the orchestrator and the app's own dev script agree on.
`repo` is what .gitmodules pins. A system whose repo is owned by someone else
is marked `"upstream": true` — it is tracked read-only and never pushed to.

systems.name: The Connected Suite
systems.purpose: The lender realm. Lending console, customer portal, analytics studio, PeopleHub, Ledgerly and ConnectDesk — six front doors, one BirgenAI ID.

domains: microeazy.servicesuitecloud.com  — CANONICAL. / is the borrower app (installed PWA start_url); /login is the lender staff door.
connectedsuite.servicesuitecloud.com — alias onto the same deployment
deploy.note: Deployed from the BirgenAI_LMS repo with its environment already mapped. The LOCAL FOLDER was renamed to connected-suite; the remote, the Vercel project and every env var are untouched, because Vercel builds from the repo and has never seen this folder name. Every subdomain above is the SAME deployment — src/proxy.ts rewrites the bare host to that system's branded door. SUITE_COOKIE_DOMAIN=.servicesuitecloud.com is what makes one sign-in carry across all of them.

systems.name: The Interchange
systems.purpose: A federated data exchange for Kenyan lenders. Members query each other in real time through a consent-gated broker; nothing is pooled, and identity is destroyed at the edge before anything crosses a boundary.

preDev.why: Starts the local PGlite Postgres the console connects to. Detached, and a no-op when it is already up.

signIn.label: Operator access code
signIn.note: Gate → Access Code → your four-digit code. Super admin code is set with `npm run operator -- create`.

signIn.label: Member certificate
signIn.note: Ed25519, signed by the member's node. The production door.

systems.database: Local PGlite via `prisma dev` on :51214 — DATABASE_URL. PRODUCTION: its own Supabase project, NEVER the Suite's. The Registry is a separate trust domain — it holds consent records and the audit trail for competing lenders, and the whole architectural claim is that the broker cannot be read from a member's own systems. Sharing a database would make a Suite credential a Registry credential. Set DATABASE_URL to the pooled string (:6543, ?pgbouncer=true) and DIRECT_URL to the direct one (:5432) for migrations.

deploy.note: THE 404 IS THIS FIELD. The repo has no package.json at its root — the Next app is at apps/interchange-console — so a Vercel project left on the default Root Directory finds nothing to build and serves a 404 with no build error to explain it. Set Root Directory to apps/interchange-console in Project Settings → General. Needs its OWN database, never the Suite's: see the database field.

systems.name: Micro Eazy
systems.purpose: The borrower realm. One installable app: verify once, apply, track and repay — routed by the Exchange to a licensed lender who funds you.
systems.database: none — talks to ServiceSuite / the Suite over HTTP

deploy.note: A flat Vite project — Root Directory is the repo root. vercel.json rewrites everything to / for client-side routing, and /api/* to the Suite at lms.servicesuitecloud.com so the borrower's SameSite=Lax cookie stays same-origin. THE DOMAIN IS SETTLED: portal.servicesuitecloud.com is this project's, microeazy.servicesuitecloud.com is the SUITE's. They are different labels because only one Vercel project can hold a hostname, and the label is reserved in connected-suite/src/lib/suite/hosts.ts so no lender can be issued it. AS OF 2026-09-01 portal.servicesuitecloud.com IS LIVE and serving this project — the domain is attached and the earlier no-DNS-record note above is superseded. This app is slated for REPLACEMENT by the 'app' system below; see micro-eazy-app/DEPLOY.md for why that cutover has not happened, and keep this project deployed until it has — it is the rollback.

systems.provenance: Copied from TallamTitus/micromart-client-pwa. Re-homed under this account as its own repo so it can be deployed and evolved independently.

systems.name: Micro Eazy (rebuild)
systems.purpose: The borrower realm, rebuilt. Same promise as 'pwa' — verify once, apply, track and repay — designed phone-first rather than adapted down from a dashboard theme.
systems.database: none — talks to the Suite over HTTP

deploy.note: NOT DEPLOYED, AND NOT YET DEPLOYABLE AS A REPLACEMENT. The scaffolding is complete — vercel.json proxies /api/* to lms.servicesuitecloud.com and falls back to the SPA shell, and vite-plugin-pwa emits a worker whose autoUpdate/clientsClaim/skipWaiting combination is what lets it displace the worker the 'pwa' project has already registered on customer devices (a service worker is replaced by another worker at the same scope, never by deploying different files). What is missing is the APP: there is no sign-in or OTP screen, and every screen except ProductChoice renders src/lib/api/samples.ts — one fictional customer. Taking portal.servicesuitecloud.com today would show every borrower a balance that is not theirs and leave them unable to sign in or repay. Wire src/lib/api/portal.ts through the screens first; then move the domain off the 'pwa' project, since only one Vercel project can hold a hostname.

systems.provenance: Written from scratch beside 'pwa', on port 5174 so the two can be run side by side and compared. Not related to TallamTitus/micromart-client-pwa.

systems.name: PBX Authentication
systems.purpose: Call-centre telephony authentication worker. Backs ConnectDesk's softphone against the PBX.
systems.database: SQL Server via App.config connection string

deploy.note: A background Worker Service, not a web app — it has no port and no browser surface.

systems.provenance: Third-party repo (skegode). Pinned read-only as a submodule: fork it before you need to push.

$comment: WHAT EACH SYSTEM COSTS TO RUN. Read by doctor.mjs and dev.mjs so the two
cannot disagree, and kept here for the same reason ports are: it is the
number you have to change when a system's shape changes.
The gap between the two modes is the whole point. `next dev` on Turbopack
holds the module graph, the compiler and the HMR server in memory and
settles near 1.9 GB per app. `next start` serves a build that is already on
disk and settles near 0.3 GB. On an 8 GB laptop that is the difference
between running the ecosystem and watching Windows page until it stops
repainting — which reads as a crash, not as a shortage.
Measured on Next 16 / Vite 7 with the Suite's route count. Re-measure with
Task Manager against a warmed server, not a cold one; Turbopack climbs for
about a minute after the first request.

portMap.$comment: Reserved so a new system does not collide. Claim the next free one here BEFORE you write the entry above.
